STATUS: HEALTHY

`pnpm run generate` + `pnpm run types` both pass cleanly. No existing errors to work around.

## FILES

- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/agent/components/AgentMessage.tsx (whole file, 62 lines) — TARGET; currently has `agent-msg__cards` placeholder div at lines 33-37 with comment "EventCard/ReminderCard/RouteSummaryCard render here in a later bead"
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/agent/components/ChatPanel.tsx:13-31, 78-127 — builds `toolCalls` payload sent to AgentMessage; see `ToolCallLite` shape
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/agent/types.ts:22-50 — EventType/EventStatus/ReminderStatus enums + all Zod schemas
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/agent/llm.ts:25-30 — `ToolCallResult` shape returned by `/agent/chat`
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/agent/llm.ts:62-109 — how server extracts events/reminders from tool-result `data` (look-alike shape: `data.event`, `data.reminder`, `data.events[]`, `data.reminders[]`, or `result.data` itself)
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/agent/server-functions/chat.ts:14-20 — `ChatResult` includes optional `events`/`reminders` arrays but route returns only `{reply, toolCalls}` currently (see handlers/index.ts isn't passing them through — verify in routes.tsx line 62-63, it spreads full result via `jsonResponse(result)`, so `events`/`reminders` DO come back alongside `reply` + `toolCalls`)
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/agent/handlers/route.ts:159-167 — `optimizeDay` ToolResult shape: `{routeId, route: OptimizedRoute, events, totalTime}`
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/agent/handlers/reminder.ts:71-91 — dismissReminder handler signature
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/agent/styles.css:177-223 — AgentMessage bubble + `.agent-msg__cards` container already styled (gap: var(--space-2))
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/route-calculator/components/PropertyCard.tsx (whole file) — visual reference for card aesthetic
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/route-calculator/styles.css:262-343 — `.btn-base`, `.btn-primary`, `.btn-danger`, `.btn-outline-*` (3px border, 4px offset box-shadow, uppercase, letter-spacing 1px)
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/route-calculator/styles.css:347-360 — `.card-base` (white bg, 3px border, 4px 4px shadow, radius 0)
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/route-calculator/styles.css:38-114 — design tokens (colors, spacing, radii, tap targets)
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/route-calculator/types.ts:4-44 — Property, RouteItem, OptimizedRoute shapes (dates are real `Date` after restore)
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/prisma/schema.prisma:282-359 — Event/Reminder/EventType/EventStatus/ReminderStatus
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/worker.tsx:96,125 — agent at `/agent/*`, route-calculator at `/route/*`
- /home/ptre/code/github/routefast/src/addons/route-calculator/routes.tsx (whole file) — only `/` and `/api/export/:format`; no query-param handshake for preloaded route

## DATA SHAPES

From `@generated/prisma` (schema-derived, fields above):

```ts
// Event (prisma model, flattened)
interface Event {
  id: string; userId: string; tenantId: string;
  title: string;
  type: "SHOWING"|"CLOSING"|"INSPECTION"|"APPRAISAL"|"LAWYER"|"TITLE"|"MEETING"|"OPEN_HOUSE"|"DEADLINE"|"OTHER";
  date: string;  // "YYYY-MM-DD"
  time: string;  // "HH:MM"
  durationMinutes: number;
  address: string|null; coordinates: string|null; sourceUrl: string|null;
  contactName: string|null; contactPhone: string|null; contactEmail: string|null;
  notes: string|null; metadata: string|null;
  status: "SCHEDULED"|"COMPLETED"|"CANCELLED";
  routeId: string|null;
  createdAt: Date; updatedAt: Date;
}

// Reminder
interface Reminder {
  id: string; userId: string; tenantId: string; eventId: string|null;
  message: string;
  remindAt: Date;  // wire = string (JSON)
  status: "PENDING"|"SENT"|"DISMISSED";
  metadata: string|null; createdAt: Date;
}
```

Current `toolCalls` arriving at AgentMessage (from ChatPanel → /agent/chat):

```ts
interface ToolCallLite {
  id: string;
  name: string;  // "createEvent" | "listEvents" | "createReminder" | ... | "optimizeDay" | "exportItinerary" etc.
  result?: { needsConfirmation?: boolean; preview?: unknown } | null;
}
```

NOTE the **gap**: current `ToolCallLite` in ChatPanel.tsx:13-17 only forwards `needsConfirmation` + `preview`. Full `ToolCallResult` from llm.ts:25-30 is `{id, name, input, result: ToolResult}` where `ToolResult = {ok, data?, needsConfirmation?, preview?, warning?, error?}`. **[GAP routefast-mol-7dl]** To render EventCard/ReminderCard from tool output, ChatPanel must forward the full `result` (incl. `ok`, `data`, `warning`) — not just the slim preview fields. Also the chat.ts result already returns top-level `events`/`reminders` arrays that could be used directly (see llm.ts:83-109 for the aggregation logic).

## DISMISS ENDPOINT

**[GAP routefast-mol-7dl]** There is NO dedicated HTTP endpoint for dismiss. `dismissReminder` only exists as an agent tool (handlers/reminder.ts:71-91) callable via `/agent/chat` with a natural-language message that triggers the tool. Two options for ReminderCard quick-action button:

1. Send `/agent/chat` a canned message like `"Dismiss reminder <id>"` — simple, consistent with confirm flow (see ChatPanel.tsx:143-146 which does `sendMessage(CONFIRM_MESSAGE)`). LLM-gated, slower, costs a turn.
2. Add new route `/agent/reminders/:id/dismiss` (POST) alongside existing routes.tsx handlers — direct, fast, no LLM round-trip. Recommend this; mirrors handler pattern at lines 132-155 (`/badge`).

Implementer should pick (2) and add to src/addons/agent/routes.tsx — ~15 lines reusing `requireAuth`+`requireTenant`+`dismissReminder` from handlers/reminder.ts.

## STYLING

Retro comic book tokens already defined in route-calculator/styles.css and used by agent/styles.css. Reuse:

- Card shell: match `.card-base` pattern (white bg, `3px solid var(--text-primary)`, `box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.15)`, `border-radius: 0`). Can add new classes to agent/styles.css like `.agent-card`, `.agent-card--event`, `.agent-card--reminder`, `.agent-card--route`.
- Buttons: copy `.btn-base` pattern (3px border, uppercase, `letter-spacing: 1px`, 4px offset shadow, translate on hover/active). Or reuse agent/styles.css `.agent-msg__confirm-btn` which is already comic-book-ish.
- Container: existing `.agent-msg__cards` already provides vertical flex gap — put cards inside it.
- Design tokens available: `--accent-electric` (blue), `--accent-success` (green), `--accent-danger` (red), `--accent-warning` (amber), `--text-primary`, `--bg-glass-elevated`, `--space-{1..16}`, `--radius-{sm,md,lg}`, `--tap-{sm,md,lg}`, `--text-{xs..4xl}`.
- Fonts: title use `'Archivo Black'` (see chat-panel__title) or `'Bebas Neue'` (see chat-fab__badge) for retro headline; body uses default inherit.

## APPROACH

1. **Widen `ToolCallLite`** in ChatPanel.tsx:13-17 and `AgentMessageProps.toolCalls` in AgentMessage.tsx:8-12 to carry full `ToolResult`: `{ok, data, needsConfirmation, preview, warning, error}`. Result already arrives on the wire (handlers/index.ts → llm.ts pushes full ToolResult into `ToolCallResult.result`, and routes.tsx:62 returns entire object via `jsonResponse(result)`).
2. **Create three card components** (all "use client", in src/addons/agent/components/):
   - `EventCard.tsx` — renders from `Event` (title, type badge, date, time, address, contact). Quick actions: "View in Calendar" (link), "Cancel" (sends canned chat msg or future endpoint).
   - `ReminderCard.tsx` — renders from `Reminder` (message, remindAt formatted). Quick action: "Dismiss" button POSTs to new `/agent/reminders/:id/dismiss`.
   - `RouteSummaryCard.tsx` — renders from `optimizeDay` tool result `{routeId, route: OptimizedRoute, totalTime, events}`. Shows stop count, total time, start/end. Action: "Open route" (linking to `/route/` — see CONCERNS).
3. **Add dismiss endpoint** in src/addons/agent/routes.tsx after `/badge` handler: `route("/reminders/:id/dismiss", [requireAuth, requireTenant, async (...) => { await dismissReminder({reminderId: params.id}, ctx); }])`. Return `{ok: true}` or error.
4. **Wire cards into AgentMessage.tsx** lines 33-37: iterate `toolCalls`, switch on `call.name` + `call.result?.ok`:
   - `createEvent` / `updateEvent` (with `result.data.event` that looksLikeEvent) → EventCard
   - `listEvents` → map `result.data` (array of Event) → EventCard list (or a compact "N events" summary + expand)
   - `createReminder` (with `result.data` that looksLikeReminder) → ReminderCard
   - `listReminders` → map array → ReminderCard list
   - `optimizeDay` → RouteSummaryCard
5. **Reuse look-alike guards** from llm.ts:62-81 (duplicate as small client helpers since llm.ts is server-only — import path would pull in prisma types which are worker-only).
6. **Styles**: add `.agent-card`, `.agent-card__header`, `.agent-card__body`, `.agent-card__actions`, `.agent-card__pill` classes to agent/styles.css. One variant per card type via modifier class. Mobile-first: full width within the 85%-max `.agent-msg`.
7. Remove `aria-hidden="true"` from `.agent-msg__cards` div (line 34) — current placeholder intentionally hidden.
8. Run `pnpm run types` after.

## CONCERNS

- **`aria-hidden="true"` on cards container** (AgentMessage.tsx:34) will hide content from screen readers — must remove when cards become real.
- **No `/route/` preload handshake**: route-calculator routes.tsx accepts no `?route=<id>` or body. "Open route" on RouteSummaryCard either needs (a) a query-param loader added to HomePageWrapper, or (b) scope-creep — for this bead, link to `/route/` with a param like `?routeId=<id>` and file a follow-up [GAP routefast-mol-7dl] to implement loader in HomePageWrapper. OR just hide the action for this bead.
- **`listEvents`/`listReminders` can return large arrays** — consider a collapse-when-more-than-N UI (e.g., render first 3, "+N more").
- **Tool input shape vs result shape**: for preview-stage (needsConfirmation), the shape is in `result.preview`, not `result.data.event`. Cards should handle both: when `needsConfirmation`, read `preview` (EventCard can render an event-like preview with a badge "PREVIEW"); when confirmed, read `data.event`. The existing inline Confirm/Cancel buttons (AgentMessage.tsx:39-58) already drive the confirmation flow — cards can render the preview alongside.
- **`exportItinerary` tool output is raw text** (handlers/export.ts:68-71: `{format, text}`). Optional card could render a copy button + preview of the text; not explicitly in scope though — implementer should clarify.
- **Reminder `remindAt` serialization**: llm.ts stringifies for wire (`JSON.stringify(result)`), so cards will get `remindAt` as an ISO string, not a Date — parse with `new Date(...)` for display.
- **Tenant scoping on dismiss endpoint**: the existing `dismissReminder` handler already checks `tenantId` (reminder.ts:78-83) — safe to wire directly.
- **llm tool aggregation already computes `events`/`reminders`** (llm.ts:83-109, chat.ts:14-20) at top level of chat response. Faster path: render cards from those top-level arrays rather than re-walking toolCalls. Trade-off: loses per-tool-call association (which tool produced which card) — probably fine for display.

description:
# VERIFICATION PHASE

## Goal
Validate that the implementation works correctly through automated AND manual verification.

## Task Context
The LLM brain. Wires Kimi K2.5 on Workers AI for tool resolution with confirmation flow and natural-language date handling.

## Files
- src/addons/agent/llm.ts (new)
- src/addons/agent/prompts.ts (new)
- wrangler.jsonc (modify — add AI binding prod + staging)

## Wrangler
Add to prod and staging:
  [ai]
  binding = "AI"

## Agent loop (src/addons/agent/llm.ts)
Function signature:
  runAgentLoop(args: {
    userMessage: string,
    history: Message[],
    contextSummary?: string,
    tools: ToolDef[],
    executeHandler: (name, input) => Promise<ToolResult>,
    ctx: AgentContext,
  }): Promise<{ reply: string, toolCalls: ToolCallResult[], events?: Event[], reminders?: Reminder[] }>

Logic:
1. Build messages array: system prompt (from prompts.ts with dynamic context) + context summary (if present) + recent history + user message.
2. Call env.AI.run('@cf/moonshot/kimi-k2.5', { messages, tools })
3. Parse response. If tool_calls: execute each via executeHandler, append tool role result messages, loop (max 5 iterations).
4. If text response: return as reply with accumulated toolCalls.
5. Track created events/reminders across tool calls to return in response.

Tool definitions for all 10 handlers in OpenAI-compatible format (name, description, parameters JSON schema from Zod schemas).

## System prompt (src/addons/agent/prompts.ts)
Template function that takes { user, preferences, counts (today events, pending reminders), now }:
- Persona: helpful real estate assistant, professional but conversational
- Current date/time in user's timezone
- List all tools and when to use them
- Rules:
  - Always resolve relative dates to absolute before calling tools ('Thursday' → '2026-04-16')
  - If date is ambiguous, ask user to clarify
  - For create/update mutations: present preview and ask confirmation before calling with confirmed=true
  - For cancel: ALWAYS confirm — destructive
  - When creating events, mention if auto-reminder will be created (based on user preferences)
- Dynamic context: user name, today's event count, pending reminder count

## Verification
1. 'what do I have today?' → list_events call with correct date filter
2. 'schedule showing at 123 Elm Thursday 2pm' → createEvent preview + needsConfirmation
3. 'yes' → createEvent with confirmed=true, Event + auto-reminder created
4. 'optimize Thursday' → list_events then optimizeDay
5. 'remind me to call John tomorrow' → resolves 'tomorrow' correctly
6. 'cancel the Elm Street showing' → agent confirms before calling cancelEvent
7. Ambiguous 'next week' → agent asks clarification
8. 5+ tool iterations → loop terminates with a text reply
9. Context summary included when history.length > 20

title: Verify VAPID signing + push subscription + key generation
description:
# VERIFICATION PHASE

## Goal
Validate that the implementation works correctly through automated AND manual verification.

## Task Context
Web Push delivery via VAPID signing using Web Crypto API. The web-push npm library uses Node.js crypto and will NOT work on Workers — must hand-roll VAPID.

## Files
- src/addons/agent/utils/vapid.ts (new)
- src/addons/agent/server-functions/pushSubscription.ts (new)
- src/scripts/generate-vapid-keys.ts (new, one-shot CLI script)
- wrangler.jsonc (modify — document VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, VAPID_SUBJECT as secrets)

## vapid.ts
Pure Web Crypto implementation. ~80 lines.
- generateVapidJwt(audience, privateKey, subject): signs ES256 JWT with crypto.subtle.sign using ECDSA P-256
- encryptPush(payload, p256dh, auth): aes128gcm encryption using crypto.subtle
- sendPushNotification(subscription, payload, env): constructs request, signs, encrypts, POSTs to subscription.endpoint with Authorization: vapid header + TTL + Content-Encoding
Reference: RFC 8030 (Web Push), RFC 8292 (VAPID), RFC 8291 (aes128gcm content encoding)

## pushSubscription.ts ('use server')
- subscribePush(subscription: PushSubscriptionJSON): save to DB (PushSubscription table from data-model bead). One active subscription per user — upsert on userId.
- unsubscribePush(): delete subscription for current user.
- sendPush(userId, payload, env): lookup user's subscription from DB, call sendPushNotification() from vapid.ts. Return success/failure. Handle 404/410 (expired subscription) by deleting it.

## generate-vapid-keys.ts
Standalone Node script:
- Use node crypto.generateKeyPairSync('ec', { namedCurve: 'P-256' })
- Export public key in uncompressed raw format (base64url)
- Export private key in PKCS8 (base64url)
- Print with instructions: 'Run wrangler secret put VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY' etc.

## wrangler.jsonc
Add comment in vars documenting required secrets:
  VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, VAPID_SUBJECT (mailto:admin@routefast.app)

## Verification
1. generate-vapid-keys.ts outputs valid base64url keys
2. generateVapidJwt produces ES256 JWT that validates against public key
3. Test push via Chrome DevTools > Application > Service Workers → subscription → sendPush delivers notification

title: Verify Agent chat + voice + history + badge routes
description:
# VERIFICATION PHASE

## Goal
Validate that the implementation works correctly through automated AND manual verification.

## Task Context
HTTP routes and server functions for the agent. Chat is a server function; voice is a raw HTTP route because audio Blobs don't survive RWSDK serialization.

## Files
- src/addons/agent/routes.tsx (new)
- src/addons/agent/server-functions/chat.ts (new)
- src/worker.tsx (modify — wire agent routes)

## Routes
POST /agent/chat — server function. Accepts { message: string }. Returns { reply, toolCalls, events?, reminders? }. Interruptors: requireAuth, requireTenant, apiRateLimit.

POST /agent/voice — raw HTTP route (NOT server function).
- Read request body as ArrayBuffer
- Call env.AI.run('@cf/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo', { audio: Array.from(new Uint8Array(body)) })
- Get transcription string
- Feed to same agent loop as /agent/chat
- Return { transcription, reply, toolCalls, events?, reminders? }

GET /agent/history — returns conversation history from AgentStateDO.
DELETE /agent/history — clears conversation.
GET /agent/badge — returns { events, reminders } today/pending counts.

## Server function (src/addons/agent/server-functions/chat.ts)
'use server'
export async function chat(message: string) {
  const { ctx, env } = requestInfo
  if (!ctx.user || !ctx.tenant) throw new Error('Auth required')
  const prefs = await getPreferences(ctx.user.id)
  const doId = env.AGENT_STATE_DO.idFromName(ctx.user.id)
  const stub = env.AGENT_STATE_DO.get(doId)
  const history = await stub.getHistory(20)
  const summary = await stub.getContextSummary()
  const result = await runAgentLoop({
    userMessage: message,
    history,
    contextSummary: summary,
    tools: ALL_TOOLS,
    executeHandler: makeExecuteHandler({ db, userId: ctx.user.id, tenantId: ctx.tenant.id, userPreferences: prefs, env }),
    ctx: { db, userId: ctx.user.id, tenantId: ctx.tenant.id, userPreferences: prefs, env },
  })
  await stub.addMessage('user', message)
  await stub.addMessage('assistant', result.reply, result.toolCalls)
  await stub.pruneAndSummarize(env)
  return result
}

## Wire in worker.tsx
prefix('/agent', agentRoutes) after auth context loading.

## Verification

title: Commit Event + Reminder domain tool handlers
description:
# COMMIT PHASE

## Goal
Create a clean git commit with the changes.

## Task Context
Pure-function domain handlers for Event and Reminder CRUD with confirmation flow, time-conflict detection, and auto-reminder creation.

## Files
- src/addons/agent/types.ts (new — AgentContext, ToolResult types, Zod schemas)
- src/addons/agent/handlers/event.ts (new)
- src/addons/agent/handlers/reminder.ts (new)

## AgentContext type
{ db, userId, tenantId, userPreferences, env }

## ToolResult type
{ ok: boolean, data?: any, needsConfirmation?: boolean, preview?: any, warning?: string, error?: string }

## Event handlers (src/addons/agent/handlers/event.ts)
- createEvent(input, ctx):
  - Input: type, title, date, time, durationMinutes?, address?, coordinates?, sourceUrl?, contactName?, contactPhone?, contactEmail?, notes?, metadata?, confirmed? (boolean)
  - If !confirmed: query existing events for date, detect time overlap (using time + durationMinutes), return preview + needsConfirmation:true with warning if overlap.
  - If confirmed: create Event in DB scoped to tenant. If ctx.userPreferences.autoReminder === true, also create Reminder at (event datetime - autoReminderMinutes). Return created Event.
- listEvents(input: { dateRange?, type?, status?, hasAddress? }, ctx): flexible filters, tenant-scoped, returns Events array.
- updateEvent(input: { eventId, fields, confirmed? }, ctx): confirmation for mutations. Validate event belongs to tenant.
- cancelEvent(input: { eventId, confirmed? }, ctx): requires confirmed. Sets status=CANCELLED and dismisses linked Reminders (status=DISMISSED).

## Reminder handlers (src/addons/agent/handlers/reminder.ts)
- createReminder(input: { message, remindAt, eventId? }, ctx): create standalone or event-linked reminder. If eventId provided, verify event belongs to tenant.
- listReminders(input: { status?, dateRange? }, ctx): tenant-scoped.
- dismissReminder(input: { reminderId }, ctx): set status=DISMISSED. Validate ownership.

All handlers: Zod validate input, throw descriptive errors, scope all queries to ctx.tenantId.

## Verification
1. pnpm run types passes
2. createEvent without confirmed returns needsConfirmation + preview
3. createEvent with confirmed creates Event
4. createEvent with autoReminder=true also creates Reminder at correct offset
5. createEvent detects time conflict with existing SCHEDULED event and returns warning
6. listEvents filters by type, dateRange, hasAddress correctly
7. cancelEvent requires confirmed, dismisses linked reminders
8. Reminder handlers validate event ownership when eventId provided
9. Cross-tenant queries never return other tenant's data

## Instructions

1. **Review changes** - Run `git diff` to see all modifications
2. **Stage relevant files** - Only include files related to this task
3. **Write commit message** - Follow conventional commits format
4. **Create commit** - Use the commit skill or git directly

## Commit Message Format
```
<type>(<scope>): <description>

<body with details>

Refs: <bead-id>
```

Types: feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore

## Output to Orchestrator

Add a comment with the commit details:
```
STATUS: DONE
COMMIT: <commit hash>
MESSAGE: <commit message summary>

ACTION: Close this step and proceed to next steps (if any).
```

When complete, close this bead with `bd close <this-bead-id>`.

- src/addons/agent/components/ChatButton.tsx (37 lines) - current simple FAB with 💬 icon + badge, toggles ChatPanel on click
- src/app/Document.tsx:18,71 - only consumer; rendered for authenticated users inside <body>
- src/addons/agent/styles.css - existing .chat-fab styles (56px via --tap-lg, bottom-right, border + shadow)
- src/addons/agent/hooks/useVoiceRecorder.ts - full recording hook w/ state (idle/recording/processing/done/error/permission-denied), amplitude, timer, start/stop/cancel
- src/addons/agent/contexts/VoiceContext.tsx - VoiceProvider wraps recorder + POSTs ArrayBuffer to /agent/voice, returns VoiceResult {transcription,reply,toolCalls,events,reminders}; exposes useVoice() + useOptionalVoice()
- src/addons/agent/components/VoiceMicButton.tsx - existing visual mic (not currently mounted anywhere in authenticated UI)
- src/addons/agent/components/voice-mic.css - pulse ring, timer, amplitude glow styles
- src/addons/agent/hooks/useBadge.ts - polls /agent/badge every 60s, returns {events,reminders}, mirrors total to navigator.setAppBadge
- src/addons/agent/routes.tsx - POST /agent/voice (ArrayBuffer, whisper, runChat) + GET /agent/badge already exist and return expected shapes
- src/addons/agent/components/ChatPanel.tsx - receives {open, onClose}; NO scroll-to-message prop exists
- src/addons/agent/components/EventCard.tsx / ReminderCard.tsx - 'use client', accept {event/reminder, preview} - reusable in AgentResponseCard

PATTERNS
- 50s retro tokens: --tap-lg (56px), --accent-electric, --accent-danger, --text-primary, --bg-glass-strong, 3px border, 4px 4px 0 shadow, animation cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1)
- Fixed overlays use z-index 40 (FAB), 50 (backdrop), 60 (panel) - response card should be ~45
- Existing chat-panel-in keyframe slides from translateY(100%) - mimic for response card
- ErrorModal pattern: focus-trap + ESC + backdrop, role=dialog. Cards use role=alert for errors.
- Pointer capture pattern for swipe-to-close in ChatPanel (handleHandlePointerDown/Up using dragStartRef)
- useVoiceRecorder.onAudioReady callback returns void|Promise - POST happens in VoiceProvider
- "use client" directive on all interactive components; no toasts (per CLAUDE.md)

APPROACH
1. ChatButton becomes 'use client' dual-mode FAB:
   - Mic icon default (🎙 or SVG), 💬 removed
   - Use useVoiceRecorder directly (no VoiceProvider needed unless desired globally) OR wrap app in VoiceProvider and use useVoice()
   - Simplest: instantiate useVoiceRecorder + POST to /agent/voice inline in ChatButton - keeps props local. But VoiceProvider already exists and does this work.
   - Recommend: mount VoiceProvider in Document.tsx around ChatButton to centralize state + onResult callback sets latest response card
   - Pointer events: track pointerdown timestamp + y position in refs. On pointerup: if hold < 500ms and no vertical drag > 30px → tap (start/stop recording). If hold >= 500ms → long-press (open ChatPanel). If swipe up (clientY delta < -40) → open ChatPanel. Clear timer on pointerup.
   - setTimeout(500) triggers long-press; cancel on early pointerup/pointermove beyond small threshold
   - Badge kept from useBadge (already correct)
   - navigator.vibrate?.(50) on recording start/stop (safely optional; iOS no-op)
   - aria-label varies with state
2. Replace 💬 with mic SVG/emoji; add recording/processing visual states (reuse .voice-mic__ring--active or add .chat-fab--recording with pulse animation)
3. Create AgentResponseCard.tsx ('use client'):
   - Props: {result: VoiceResult, onOpen: () => void, onDismiss: () => void}
   - Position: fixed, bottom: calc(var(--space-4) + var(--tap-lg) + var(--space-3) + safe-area), right: var(--space-4), max-width ~320px, z-index 45
   - Slides up from below FAB (translateY + opacity keyframe)
   - setTimeout(3000) onMount auto-dismiss; clear on unmount/tap
   - Tap → onOpen (parent opens ChatPanel with scrollTo=agentTurnId)
   - Render reply text (truncate 2 lines) + first EventCard/ReminderCard inline
   - role="status" aria-live="polite" (NOT a toast — user-initiated, dismissible, persistent affordance)
4. ChatPanel prop extension: add optional {scrollToMessageId?: string} and optional {seedMessages?: ChatTurn[]} so response card tap opens panel already showing that turn. Consider lifting messages state to a shared context OR simply pass initial turn in via prop.
5. Add CSS to styles.css: .chat-fab--recording (pulse), .agent-response-card + slide-up keyframe

CONCERNS / GAPS
- ChatPanel maintains its own messages state internally — tapping the response card to "scroll to that message" requires either (a) lifting chat state to a context, (b) adding a seed message prop, or (c) calling /agent/history on open. Option (b) is simplest if we only need to show the latest voice turn. Orchestrator should confirm expected behavior.
- VoiceProvider is currently unused in the authenticated tree. Two choices: (i) wrap <ChatButton> subtree in <VoiceProvider>, or (ii) inline useVoiceRecorder in ChatButton. (i) is cleaner since response card also needs the result.
- ChatButton is currently a server-imported client component in Document.tsx; making it the root of a provider tree means Document.tsx stays server-rendered but ChatButton children are client — confirm this pattern works with rwsdk (it does for ChatPanel already).
- Long-press + swipe discrimination on desktop mouse: use pointer events (already supported). Need to cancel long-press timer on pointercancel/pointerleave.
- No global context clash: there's no existing global keyboard/pointer listener that competes.
- /agent/voice returns 401 when unauthenticated — FAB only shows when user logged in (Document.tsx gates via showChat), so fine.
- 56px = var(--tap-lg) already. Spec says 56px — token matches.
- No existing tests — TypeScript clean only, no test suite to break.

# ORCHESTRATOR: PWA manifest + service worker + iOS meta tags

You coordinate child steps for this task.

## sw.js (vanilla JS, not bundled)
self.addEventListener('push', event => {
  const data = event.data ? event.data.json() : {}
  event.waitUntil(self.registration.showNotification(data.title, {
    body: data.body,
    icon: '/icons/icon-192.png',
    data: { url: data.url || '/route/' }
  }))
})
self.addEventListener('notificationclick', event => {
  event.notification.close()
  event.waitUntil(clients.openWindow(event.notification.data.url))
})

title: Commit Reminder cron + daily email digest via Resend
description:
# COMMIT PHASE

## Goal
Create a clean git commit with the changes.

## Task Context
Scheduled tasks: every 5min check for due reminders + fire push. Daily digest email to users who opted in. Both handled by single scheduled() handler dispatching on cron time.

## Files
- src/addons/agent/server-functions/reminderCron.ts (new)
- src/addons/agent/server-functions/dailyDigest.ts (new)
- src/addons/agent/hooks/useBadge.ts (new, 'use client')
- src/worker.tsx (modify — add scheduled handler)
- wrangler.jsonc (modify — crons, RESEND_API_KEY, DIGEST_FROM_EMAIL)

## wrangler.jsonc
Add to prod + staging:
  triggers.crons: ['*/5 * * * *', '0 12 * * *']  (every 5min + daily 12 UTC ≈ 7-8am ET)
Document secrets: RESEND_API_KEY
Add vars: DIGEST_FROM_EMAIL = 'reminders@routefast.app'

## reminderCron.ts
runReminderCron(env):
- Query Reminders where remindAt <= now AND status = PENDING
- For each: lookup PushSubscription for userId, call sendPush with { title: 'RouteFast', body: reminder.message, url: '/route/' }
- Update reminder.status = SENT
- Users without subscription still get SENT (don't block forever)

## dailyDigest.ts
runDailyDigest(env):
- Query all Users where preferences.dailyDigest = true
- For each user (in their preferences.timezone):
  - Today's events (SCHEDULED) + pending reminders for today
  - Format HTML + plain text:
    'Good morning! Today's schedule:'
    Events grouped by time with type icon, title, time, address, contact
    Pending reminders list
    'Nothing scheduled today!' if empty
    Link to https://routefast.app
  - POST to https://api.resend.com/emails with Authorization: Bearer env.RESEND_API_KEY
- NOTE: single cron time means users in other timezones get digest at different local times. Acceptable for now.

## Scheduled handler in worker.tsx
export default {
  ...existing,
  async scheduled(event, env, ctx) {
    await setupDb(env)
    if (event.cron === '*/5 * * * *') await runReminderCron(env)
    else if (event.cron === '0 12 * * *') await runDailyDigest(env)
  }
}

title: Implement VAPID signing + push subscription + key generation
description:
# IMPLEMENTATION PHASE

## Goal
Make the code changes to implement the feature/fix.

## Task Context
Web Push delivery via VAPID signing using Web Crypto API. The web-push npm library uses Node.js crypto and will NOT work on Workers — must hand-roll VAPID.

## Files
- src/addons/agent/utils/vapid.ts (new)
- src/addons/agent/server-functions/pushSubscription.ts (new)
- src/scripts/generate-vapid-keys.ts (new, one-shot CLI script)
- wrangler.jsonc (modify — document VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, VAPID_SUBJECT as secrets)

## vapid.ts
Pure Web Crypto implementation. ~80 lines.
- generateVapidJwt(audience, privateKey, subject): signs ES256 JWT with crypto.subtle.sign using ECDSA P-256
- encryptPush(payload, p256dh, auth): aes128gcm encryption using crypto.subtle
- sendPushNotification(subscription, payload, env): constructs request, signs, encrypts, POSTs to subscription.endpoint with Authorization: vapid header + TTL + Content-Encoding
Reference: RFC 8030 (Web Push), RFC 8292 (VAPID), RFC 8291 (aes128gcm content encoding)

## pushSubscription.ts ('use server')
- subscribePush(subscription: PushSubscriptionJSON): save to DB (PushSubscription table from data-model bead). One active subscription per user — upsert on userId.
- unsubscribePush(): delete subscription for current user.
- sendPush(userId, payload, env): lookup user's subscription from DB, call sendPushNotification() from vapid.ts. Return success/failure. Handle 404/410 (expired subscription) by deleting it.

## generate-vapid-keys.ts
Standalone Node script:
- Use node crypto.generateKeyPairSync('ec', { namedCurve: 'P-256' })
- Export public key in uncompressed raw format (base64url)
- Export private key in PKCS8 (base64url)
- Print with instructions: 'Run wrangler secret put VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY' etc.

## wrangler.jsonc
Add comment in vars documenting required secrets:
  VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, VAPID_SUBJECT (mailto:admin@routefast.app)

## Verification
1. generate-vapid-keys.ts outputs valid base64url keys
2. generateVapidJwt produces ES256 JWT that validates against public key
3. Test push via Chrome DevTools > Application > Service Workers → subscription → sendPush delivers notification
4. iOS Safari PWA: sendPush delivers notification via Apple Push Notification service
5. Expired subscription (410) is deleted from DB
6. No Node crypto imports — purely Web Crypto API

2. **Make focused changes** - Implement one thing at a time
3. **Follow existing patterns** - Match the codebase style

CHANGES:
- src/addons/agent/utils/vapid.ts (new, 210 lines): base64url helpers, HKDF extract/expand, generateVapidJwt (ES256 via ECDSA P-256), encryptPush (aes128gcm per RFC 8291/8188 — ECDH with ephemeral P-256, HKDF-derived CEK+NONCE, AES-GCM body with 0x02 record terminator, rfc8188 header: salt||rs||idlen||keyid), sendPushNotification (builds vapid Authorization, POSTs to endpoint, returns {status, ok, expired}).
- src/addons/agent/server-functions/pushSubscription.ts (new, 105 lines): subscribePush/unsubscribePush/getVapidPublicKey as serverAction, sendPush (server-internal, deletes expired subscriptions on 404/410).

title: Rate limit: key password reset by email+IP, not just IP
description:
## Task
Current `passwordResetRateLimit` (5 attempts / 15 min) keys by IP alone. On shared networks (office WiFi, mobile carrier NAT), one user can block others. Observed in practice hitting 429 during testing.

## Change (`src/app/interruptors/rateLimit.ts`)
Add option to include a body-derived key component. For password reset, key = `pw-reset:{ip}:{email}`. Requires reading email from request body, which means the rate limiter needs to be applied **after** parsing or implemented inside the server action.

### Recommended approach
Move rate limiting *inside* the serverAction itself rather than as an interruptor, so it can access the validated email arg:

```ts
// In passwordReset.ts requestPasswordReset, before DB work:
const ip = requestInfo.request.headers.get('cf-connecting-ip') ?? 'unknown';
if (isRateLimited(`pw-reset:${ip}:${email}`, 5, 15*60*1000)) {
  return { success: false, error: 'Too many attempts for this email. Try in 15 min.' };
}
```

Then remove `passwordResetRateLimit` from routes.ts:36 for the forgot-password route (keep it for reset-password submission which has the token in body).

Export `isRateLimited` from `rateLimit.ts` for this use.

## Test Steps
1. 6 attempts with email A from IP X → blocked on email A
2. Simultaneously attempt with email B from IP X → not blocked
3. Wait 15 min → email A unblocks

## Tradeoff
Mildly weakens defense against enumeration-via-ratelimit (attacker can test N emails each up to 5 times). Acceptable because the reset response body never reveals whether an account exists.

title: Route /user/auth — identifier-first two-step page
description:
## Task
Build the new unified auth page at `/user/auth`. Replaces separate /user/login + /user/signup. Two steps, one URL, cross-fade transition between steps.

## Route (`src/app/pages/user/routes.ts`)
Add:
```ts
route('/auth', [
  loginRateLimit, // keep existing IP rate limit as baseline
  ({ ctx }) => {
    if (ctx.user && ctx.tenant) {
      return new Response(null, { status: 302, headers: { Location: '/route/' } })
    }
  },
  AuthPage,
]),
```

## Create `src/app/pages/user/AuthPage.tsx` (client component)

### Step 1 — email input
- Single `<input type="email">`, autoFocus, autoComplete="email"
- Inline validation on Continue (empty, regex)
- Continue button calls `lookupAuthMethod(email)` server query
- Loading state on button: "Checking..."
- Below Continue button: tiny legal text "By continuing, you agree to Terms and Privacy" (inline consent, no checkbox)

### Step 2 (morph based on lookup result)
Preserve container height — reserve space equal to tallest layout, cross-fade content via CSS `transition: opacity 200ms, transform 200ms`.

Shared header on step 2:
- "Welcome back, {email}" (returning user) OR "Let's set you up, {email}" (new user)
- Small "different?" link to reset state to step 1

**2a — returning with passkey:**
```
[ 👆 Sign in with fingerprint or face ]   ← "primary" button style
(auto-triggered at 600ms; see routefast-??? [passkey auto-trigger bead])

── or ──
[ password ___ ] [ Sign in ]
[ Email me a magic link ]
Forgot password?
```

**2b — returning without passkey:**
```
[ password ___ ] [ Sign in ]
[ Email me a magic link ]
Forgot password?
```

**2c — new user:**
```
[ password ___ ] [ confirm ___ ]
[ Create account ]

── or ──
[ Email me a magic link — no password needed ]

15 free route calculations to start.
```

### Step 3 — "check your email" (after magic link sent)
- Envelope icon + halftone
- Copy: "Check your email — we sent a sign-in link to {email}. Tap the link to continue. It works for 15 minutes."
- Small button: "Wrong email? Start over" → back to step 1
- 60-second resend countdown: "Didn't get it? Resend in 0:47" → "Resend" button after countdown
- Poll for session in same browser (routefast-??? [polling bead]) — redirect to /route/ if authenticated

## Reuse server functions
- `lookupAuthMethod` (routefast-c1o)
- `loginWithPassword`, `signupWithPassword`, `startPasskeyLogin`, `finishPasskeyLogin` from existing `functions.ts`
- `requestMagicLink` (routefast-pj0)

## CSS
Create `src/app/pages/user/auth.css` — reuse login.css variables. Key classes: `.auth-page`, `.auth-container`, `.auth-step`, `.auth-step-enter/exit`, halftone-shadow, etc. Retro comic aesthetic consistent with login/signup.

## Test Steps
1. pnpm run types
2. Enter existing-user-with-password email → step 2b
3. Enter existing-user-with-passkey email → step 2a (auto-trigger will come in later bead)
4. Enter new email → step 2c, fill password, create account → /route/ with 15 credits
5. Click "email me a magic link" on any step-2 variant → step 3, email received
6. Tap "different?" → back to step 1 with email cleared
7. 21+ rapid email submissions → rate-limited message
8. Mobile viewport — layout usable

## Non-goals (handled in other beads)
- Passkey auto-trigger (next bead)
- Same-browser polling (next bead)
- Redirects from /user/login, /user/signup (next bead)

AuthPage.tsx + auth.css, routed behind loginRateLimit. Types green. Non-goals deferred: passkey auto-trigger (bfq), polling (20c), redirects (ecn).

Once `/user/auth` has been in prod and stable for 2+ weeks, delete the old `Login.tsx` and `Signup.tsx` component files. Keep the routes as 302 redirects to /user/auth (already done in routefast-ecn).

- `src/app/pages/user/Signup.tsx`

4. Visit /user/signup → 302 → /user/auth ✓

title: Audit D1-incompatible Prisma patterns ( interactive, raw SQL, etc.)
description:
## Task
D1 does not support Prisma interactive transactions (`db.$transaction(async (tx) => {...})`). Two bugs shipped to prod in the Option B rollout because of this:
- `src/app/pages/user/magicLink.ts:verifyMagicLinkCore` — hot-fixed 2026-04-19
- `src/app/pages/user/passwordReset.ts:resetPassword` — hot-fixed 2026-04-19

Error surfaced: `"Cloudflare D1 does not support interactive transactions. We recommend you to refactor your queries with that limitation in mind, and use batch transactions with prisma.$transactions([]) where applicable."`

Audit the whole codebase for other D1-incompatible Prisma patterns so nothing else silently breaks at runtime.

## What to look for

### Hard-fail patterns (will throw on any D1 call)
1. `db.$transaction(async (tx) => ...)` — interactive transaction. Fix: sequential ops with manual compensation, OR batch `db.$transaction([op1, op2, ...])` where ops are independent.
2. Nested transactions (passing `tx` into a helper that calls `tx.$transaction(...)`) — same interactive issue.
3. `prisma.$queryRaw`/`$executeRaw` with multi-statement SQL — D1 only supports single statement per call. Verify each raw call is a single statement.
4. Prisma `createMany` with `skipDuplicates: true` on D1 — not supported on SQLite adapters. Check every `createMany` call.

### Soft-fail / behavior-diff patterns
5. `findFirstOrThrow` / `findUniqueOrThrow` — supported but throws instead of returning null; confirm callers handle.
6. Implicit many-to-many relations — D1 SQLite supports them but some edge cases. Flag any.
7. JSON filters on SQLite (`path: [...]`) — limited compared to Postgres. Flag any.
8. Cursor-based pagination with `take: negative` — SQLite edge behavior.
9. `orderBy` with multiple columns that use complex expressions — worth double-check.

## Method
1. `rg -n '\$transaction\('` — list every call site
2. `rg -n '\$queryRaw|\$executeRaw'` — list every raw SQL call
3. `rg -n 'createMany'` — check for skipDuplicates
4. `rg -n 'findFirstOrThrow|findUniqueOrThrow'` — note callers
5. For each hit, verify against the D1-compatibility rules above
6. For each incompatible pattern found, either fix inline (small) or open a follow-up fix bead (large)

## Deliverable
One of the following comment patterns on this bead:
- `[summary] Audited N call sites. All compatible with D1.`
- `[summary] Audited N call sites. Found M issues at [files]. Fixed K inline, created fix beads for [ids] covering the rest.`

## Test Steps (per-fix)
1. pnpm run types
2. pnpm run dev — trigger each affected code path locally
3. Confirm no runtime "D1 does not support" errors in wrangler logs

## Why prior audit missed this
routefast-l4u audited `sessions.save()` for orphan-session bug pattern (per fresh-catch research). Different failure mode — this bead is the D1-Prisma-compat audit that should've run alongside. Going forward: any time we add a new D1-backed feature, run this audit pattern.

## Follow-up learnings to capture
If you find a pattern here that should become a permanent guardrail:
- Add a lint rule / grep check to CI
- Document in CLAUDE.md "D1 constraints" section
- Note the pattern in comments above the repaired call

- `$queryRaw`/`$executeRaw`: 3 hits — worker.tsx:36 & db.ts:25 (SELECT 1, single-statement, OK); seed.ts:10 multi-statement DELETE block (BROKEN on D1)
- `createMany`: only in prisma-middleware.ts (tenantId injector); no `skipDuplicates` anywhere

title: EPIC: Unified auth (identifier-first + magic link + deep-link ready)
description:
## Overview
Replace separate /user/login + /user/signup with a single identifier-first page /user/auth. Server detects account state on email submit, routes to the right auth method. Adds magic-link login/signup as a "magical" option that plays well with future Capacitor deep links. Keeps password as first-class (Jane uses it daily). Passkey auto-triggered for registered users with 600ms delay + graceful fallback.

## Goals
- Eliminate "Am I signing up or logging in?" confusion
- Make magic-link sign-in work today on web, seamlessly on Capacitor later
- Preserve passkey UX where it's the best method, gracefully fall back where it isn't
- Never say "passkey" to users — always "fingerprint or face"
- Reliable recovery path for orphaned passkey users (you two right now)

## Non-goals
- OTP codes (skipped per UX review — magic link wins for this app)
- Invisible / lazy registration (users already get 15 free credits post-signup)
- Unifying forgot-password into /user/auth (kept separate, distinct flow)

## Sub-beads (ship order)
Group 1 (foundation): AuthToken schema, lookupAuthMethod, copy change
Group 2 (core flow): requestMagicLink, verifyMagicLink, /user/auth, /user/magic
Group 3 (polish): passkey auto-trigger, same-browser polling, redirects
Group 4 (risk): passkey management upgrade (routefast-1f2 elevated), sessions.save() audit
Group 5 (Capacitor): native API endpoint, well-known files
Group 6 (cleanup): password nudge, retire old Login/Signup

## Success criteria
- Either of your two prod accounts can sign in from any device via password OR magic link within 15 sec
- New user can sign up via magic link, never touch a password field, land in /route/ with 15 credits
- Existing passkey users auto-triggered and logged in in ~2 sec; fallback to password when passkey broken
- Jane can sign in on her iPhone with no passcode (magic link works without keychain)
- Deep-link URL shape (/user/magic?token=) works in Safari today, will work in Capacitor without URL change

## Related (already open)
